subject: Review: Cookie tracking & privacy policy for Acme Health integration
messages:
From: Emma Rhodes <emma.rhodes@acmehealth.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Privacy Team <privacy@acmehealth.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Jun 2025 16:13:00 -0700
Subject: Cookie/pixel questions + DPIA ask for Redwood integration

Hi Laura,

Thanks for the demo last week — things are looking promising. Our privacy team asked me to follow up with a few specific questions about tracking on your hosted docs and integration pages before we proceed with the pilot:

- Do Redwood-hosted pages load any third-party marketing pixels (Facebook, Google Ads, LinkedIn, ad partners) by default, or only if the customer enables them?
- Are there any client-side cookies set by Redwood that are readable by third parties? Which cookies are persistent vs session-only?
- For analytics/telemetry collected by Redwood, is any data ever used for ad targeting or shared with ad networks?
- We need to confirm you provide a PCI/PHI-friendly DPA and Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs) for EU data flows. Can you attach your standard DPA and a statement on SCCs?
- Given we are a regulated healthcare org, our legal team is requesting a DPIA template showing what you assess for integrations that may touch PHI.

I attached our cookie mapping worksheet with the areas we flagged. Can you review and let us know the authoritative answers and any suggested language we can include in our privacy policy? If it's easier, we can schedule a short call — privacy team availability this Thur-Fri (PST).

Attachments: cookie-map.xlsx (spreadsheet, 38KB), privacy_policy_draft_v3.pdf (PDF, 120KB)

Thanks,
Emma Rhodes
Senior Privacy Counsel
Acme Health
phone: +1 415-555-0199

From: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>

Date: Tue, 10 Jun 2025 18:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Cookie/pixel questions + DPIA ask for Redwood integration

Hi Emma — thanks for the clear checklist and the cookie map. Looping in Markus (Legal) and Evelyn (Solutions) to confirm details and provide the DPIA template. Initial answers below — I'll follow up with docs and a proposed privacy-policy blurb by EOD tomorrow. If that doesn't work, happy to jump on a 20-min call Thu-Fri.

Quick answers (high level):
- Marketing pixels: Redwood-hosted product pages and DX/marketing pages do not load third-party marketing pixels by default for customer content. We do load a small set of telemetry/analytics pixels on our public marketing site; however, any marketing pixels related to a customer's integration are only enabled if the customer explicitly configures them in their account and consents via the console.
- Cookies: We set a few first-party cookies for session management and product UX. We do not expose those cookies to ad networks. Persistent cookies are only used for login/session preferences; no identifiers are shared with advertisers.
- Analytics/telemetry: Runtime telemetry used for service quality (latency/cost) is internal. We do not feed telemetry into ad targeting systems.
- DPA & SCCs: We have a standard DPA and offer SCCs for EU transfers; Markus will attach the DPA and confirm language.
- DPIA: We can provide a DPIA template and a short checklist that maps controls (encryption, access controls, audit logs) to typical healthcare concerns.

Action items:
- Markus: attach DPA, SCC statement, and DPIA template.
- Evelyn: confirm cookie persistence names and provide a short policy blurb.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Director, Strategic Accounts (Redwood Inference)
[Attachment: redwood_cookie_snippets.txt]

Laura / Monica — forwarding Emma's note and Laura's reply. Drafting the materials now; attaching the DPA (standard), a short SCC confirmation statement, and a DPIA template we can send to Acme. Below are suggested snippets for the privacy policy and the cookie table — please pick the tone you want me to send to Emma.

Suggested privacy blurb for policy (concise, customer-facing):
"When you integrate with Redwood, customer-configured third-party tracking (for marketing or analytics) is only loaded when explicitly enabled by the customer. Redwood’s hosted pages do include limited first-party cookies for authentication and session management; these cookies are not shared with advertising networks. Redwood’s telemetry is used solely to operate and improve the service and is not used for ad targeting"

Cookie table examples (to paste into your draft):
- _rdw_session (first-party, session): session management, expires on browser close
- _rdw_pref (first-party, persistent, 30 days): UI preferences
- analytics_rid (first-party, persistent, 180 days): aggregated product telemetry id (not shared with third parties)

DPA & SCCs: attached DPA is our standard template. We execute SCCs for customers with EU data flows; we also support customer-specific addenda where necessary for healthcare/regulatory requirements.

DPIA template: attached — includes sections on data flows, risk assessment, mitigation, and mapping to controls (encryption at rest/in transit, RBAC, logging/retention). Note: for integrations touching PHI, we recommend a short joint-data-flow session to capture the exact processing activities.

Attachments: redwood_standard_dpa.pdf (PDF, 85KB), redwood_scc_statement.txt (text, 3KB), redwood_dpia_template.docx (DOCX, 64KB)

Please tell me if you want this packaged as a single email back to Acme or if we should route the DPA through contracts/legal for signature.

-Markus
Head of Legal (Redwood Inference)
